column1: # Sonar rules that a StyleBro or SDK rule fixes (docs/migrating.md, "Coming from SonarQube"). Tab-separated:
# Sonar id, the rule that fixes it, mode (on: the rule is turned on; option: only the setting, the rule must be on already),
# the settings written with it ('; '-separated, or -), a note for the report (or -). Mode none: not covered, the note says why (rule -).
# Then per Sonar version (SonarAnalyzer.CSharp): the first one with the rule (or -: 9.16 or older) and the first one
# with it in "Sonar way" when that changed (or -), from the rule metadata in github.com/SonarSource/sonar-dotnet
# (analyzers/rspec/cs at the release tags). Older versions don't have the rule, or don't turn it on by default.

column5: BRO1309 is stricter: it also checks events and enum members, and names with '_' inside, which S100 accepts
BRO1309 is stricter: it also checks enums, delegates and test classes ('fooTests'), which S101 accepts
CA1052 is stricter: it reports classes with a private or protected constructor, a static member of their own type (a singleton) or a non-static nested type, which S1118 accepts
IDE0075 and IDE0100 are stricter: IDE0075 also simplifies constants and 'default', and 'c ? true : true'; IDE0100 also inside a conditional with a throw, which S1125 accepts
IDE0059 is stricter: it also removes dead stores to variables that are used later, which S1481 accepts
IDE0059 is stricter: it also removes initial values like 0, null and "", stores to captured variables, unused 'out var' and pattern variables, which S1854 accepts
IDE0004 removes more casts than S1905 (an upcast, a numeric conversion), and it has no option to narrow it
CA1822 is stricter: it also reports members with attributes, empty and recursive methods, events and members of generic types, which S2325 accepts
CA1805 is stricter: it also reports 'default', 'new Guid()', enums set to 0 and nullable value types set to null, which S3052 accepts
CA1852's fix also seals private nested classes with protected members (CS0628 warnings: 144 in SmartEnum)
CA1012 is stricter: it also reports a public constructor in another part of a partial abstract class, which S3442 accepts
only overloads with the same access stay together, as Sonar's S4136 asks; between accesses StyleCop's SA1202 order stays
